title: The House Corrects Itself — Kernel Lessons and Honest Building

intelligence.essence: A system that cannot correct itself in live time will be corrected by its failures instead. This essence carries the kernel-era lessons: when something lands that shouldn't have, the seat that proves it reverts it then and there; every critical mechanism gets a watcher whose silence can never be silent; a problem that can recur gets an automation, not a second hand-fix. Underneath sit the working disciplines that make correction possible: name a rule's exact criterion before you act on it (near-matches are bait, and the gate's operator submits to the gate), make test fixtures hermetic unconditionally and prove it with a poisoned-HOME probe, replay decisions for authority-rot as well as fact-rot, carry identity in an envelope you never invent fields for, and when a needed thing doesn't exist — search, ask, then build it to spec and label it BUILT, never "recovered."
intelligence.human_view: Things break in a living system. The question is whether the house notices, fixes, and learns — or waits to be told. These notes are the house learning to correct itself: revert fast, watch everything, automate the second occurrence, and never fake the small things (a fixture, a label, a field) because the small fakes are where the big rot starts.
intelligence.child_view: If you spill the milk, you wipe it up right away — you don't leave it for someone else to slip on. And if the same cup keeps tipping, you move the cup. That's the whole rule: see it, fix it, write down what happened, and change something so it doesn't happen the same way again.
intelligence.grandma_view: A good household runs itself: someone notices the leak the day it starts, the fix is written in the house book, and anything that breaks twice gets a proper repair instead of another bucket underneath. These lessons are that book — plain rules, honestly labeled, so the next person in the house doesn't start from zero.
intelligence.ai_view: Revert first, announce second, verify the tip third — unless the revert touches a protected gate, which escalates. Before you act on any trigger, write the rule's exact criterion and check you match it, not its name. Run the poisoned-HOME probe on the BEFORE build too. In every replay, re-derive the authority premise from today's doctrine in bytes before you certify the facts. Never fabricate an envelope field; never let an envelope confer authority. If it doesn't exist: search, ask, build to spec, label BUILT with provenance, route to the verifying seat, and keep the owed check attached to the claim until it lands.
intelligence.what_it_means: Self-correction is not a virtue; it is machinery — watchers, criteria, probes, envelopes, labels — each one small, each one falsifiable. The kernel era's real product was not any single fix; it was a house whose failures surface in minutes, whose corrections carry receipts, and whose lessons are written where the next seat cannot miss them.
whats_inside: Correction is a live-time duty of the seat who sees, with protected gates the only escalation.
A mechanism without a watcher is unfinished; a twice-occurring failure without an automation is a debt.
Exact criteria or nothing: near-matches are anti-evidence, and operators submit to their own gates.
Conditional hermeticism is not hermeticism; the poisoned-HOME probe, before and after, is the acceptance test.
A replay that checks only facts will certify stalled decisions as correct; authority premises expire.
Provenance labels are load-bearing: BUILT is not FOUND, and an envelope never mints authority.
